cards.explanation: The answer is things consistent with sound doctrine, friends. Paul says, "But as for you, speak the things that are consistent with sound doctrine." He doesn't say speak what's trendy or what gets a cheer. He says speak what matches the teaching, and Titus doesn't need a committee meeting to do that.

The answer is young, friends. Paul says the older women are to be teachers of good, "In this way they can train the young women…" So the older women have something to hand down, and the younger women are the ones receiving it. It's one generation passing the recipe to the next.

The reason Paul gives is so the word of God won't be discredited, friends. He says all this is "…so that the word of God will not be discredited." The way they live is tied to how the word of God is seen. Paul doesn't make it complicated, and he doesn't need to.

The answer is True, friends, so count it up. For the older men, Paul lists a whole run of things: temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance. For the younger men, it's one line: "…urge the younger men to be self-controlled." Short and to the point.

The answer is an example to follow, friends. Paul says, "…show yourself to be an example by doing good works." Titus isn't just supposed to tell people what to do, he's supposed to be what he's telling them. People watch the leader more than they listen to him. I know a stamper who learned that watching Mother Miller press dough.

The answer is False, friends. Paul writes, "In everything, show yourself to be an example by doing good works." He doesn't cut it down to only the big moments. The small moments count too, and it's the small ones nobody's clapping for.

The answer is that they'll be left ashamed with nothing bad to say, friends. Paul wants Titus's teaching above reproach "…so that anyone who opposes us will be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us." If the critic looks for something to pounce on and comes up empty, that's a quiet kind of win.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says "…not stealing from them, but showing all good faith…" There's no allowance for taking a little here and there. It's a clear line, and it comes with all good faith instead.

The answer is that it makes the teaching beautiful in every way, friends. Paul says "…in every respect they will adorn the teaching about God our Savior." Adorn is a decorating word, so their good faith is like decoration on the teaching. And he says in EVERY respect, so none of it is left plain.

The answer is ungodliness and worldly passions, friends. Paul says grace "…instructs us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions…" So grace isn't only a gift we receive, it's a teacher that points us in a direction. And he follows it right away with how to live.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says grace teaches us "…to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age…" That's now, with no delay built in. Nobody has to wait until they're older, wiser, or have more free time.

The answer is Jesus Christ our Savior, friends. Paul says we await "…the blessed hope and glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ." Our hope has a name, and the name is Jesus. Everything else in the passage leans toward that.

The answer is lawlessness, friends. Paul says Jesus "…gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness…" Notice the word ALL. He gave Himself for us, and that's a gift big enough to carry the whole thing.

The answer is good deeds, friends. Paul says Jesus purifies "…a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds." Zealous means eager, so these folks aren't dragging their feet. They're the ones first in line to help with the dishes.

The answer is True, friends, it's both. Paul says to speak these things "…as you encourage and rebuke with all authority." Rebuke sits right next to encourage in the same sentence. Titus gets the two jobs together.
The answer is despise, friends. Paul says, "Let no one despise you." Titus is to speak with all authority, and Paul doesn't want anyone looking down on him. Strong last word to Titus in this chapter.
